A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same RecLM work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendix 6 are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments on MIND, Netflix, and Industrial data, including performance comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and a profile-generation case study in Section 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–4, with experimental details in Appendix 6.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.4 and Appendix 6.6 retain identical feature/profile fusion, two-turn collaborative instruction tuning, reward-model training, and PPO refinement procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate news recommendation on MIND and Industrial data and movie recommendation on Netflix. Full-shot and zero-shot cold-start coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BiasMF, NCF, LightGCN, SGL, and SimGCL with the same comparison variants. Figure 3 retains the same Base, LLMRec, and RecLM comparisons.

E3.justification: Chronological splits, dataset counts in Table 4, full-shot/zero-shot definitions, all-rank evaluation, Recall/NDCG cutoffs, and model configurations are identical.

E4.justification: The instruction-tuning ablations in Figure 2, user/item augmentation ablations in Table 2, efficiency analysis, and reinforcement-learning case study in Figure 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same significance markers and p-value threshold of 0.05. Neither version changes the reporting of repeated runs, seeds, or uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–3 and graphical findings in Figures 2–4 match. For example, full-shot LightGCN with RecLM on MIND retains Recall@20 of 0.0788 and NDCG@20 of 0.0337.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the mathematical formulation of the method, and the time-complexity analysis in Section 3.5 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about model-agnostic integration, collaborative instruction tuning, reinforcement-learning refinement, and improved recommendation under data scarcity.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning collaborative information, noise, over-smoothing, and offline deployment are unchanged. Appendix 6.7 retains the same proposed multimodal and smaller-model extensions.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same implementation link, A100 hardware information, LoRA configuration, recommender hyperparameters, and instruction templates in Appendices 6.5–6.6.

R1.justification: Section 4 and the bibliography are identical, including the positioning relative to LLMRec, RLMRec, InstructRec, and TALLRec. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 26 December 2024, to v3, dated 1 June 2025. The paper's prose, headings, terminology, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–4, and the body layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–16 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only within the arXiv margin stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information of v1, including the appendices. The updated arXiv stamp and added manuscript self-link do not materially change the paper's clarity, rigor, or overall quality.
